messages:
mike_support: FYI support ticket from FinX — they need streaming chat that can call customer tools and stream partial structured outputs (JSON frames) while the tool is executing. Says current SDK can’t handle incremental fncall responses.

mike_sales: This is flagged as a deal blocker for their onboarding. committed spend if we ship a reliable path.

jake_pm: Can you paste the ticket example? need concrete contract + breakpoints to evaluate effort.

mike_support: Paste from user: 
```
User: call /price-check with {"symbol":"ACME"} -> tool starts heavy compute, returns incremental price updates as they arrive:
{"type":"update","price":123.4}
...more frames...
{"type":"final","price":124.1, "metadata":{...}}
```
They want the model to stream assistant messages that include those frames as function outputs, and allow client to consume partial frames for UI updates.

sarah_eng: Short notes from infra side: streaming fncall + structured frames looks similar to the streaming partial-fncall work we scoped last quarter. Main gaps: (1) schema delimiting (we need stable framing) (2) backpressure/cancel semantics (how to cancel an in-progress tool and notify model) (3) routing/compat with our batching kernel logic.

ben_sre: Important to call out SLO impacts — long-running tool calls may keep GPU slots. we should define fallback (short-circuit to non-streaming variant or lower tier) and quotas. Also TLS + proxying considerations for customer-hosted tools.

anna_product: Proposed acceptance criteria (for triage):
- AC1: API supports streaming assistant tokens interleaved with structured function frames (JSON) with a clear frame boundary marker.
- AC2: Client can request "partialFrames=true" and receive intermediate frames before final function return.
- AC3: Cancellation API: client can signal cancel, we propagate to tool (if integrated) and close stream with an error frame.
- AC4: Backwards compatible: existing non-streaming fncall behavior unchanged.

jake_pm: Prioritization request: classify as P0/P1? sales says deal. engineering estimate?

sarah_eng: Rough t-shirt: M -> L depending on how much of tool integration we standardize. If we reuse existing stream framing + small schema additions, ~3 sprint -> P1. If we need new orchestrator changes for cancel+quota, pushes to ~6 sprints -> P0 for enterprise.

mike_sales: FinX wants a pilot in 6 weeks. willing to do partnership pilot (engineering time + test dataset). If we can promise pilot with reduced scope (only streaming assistant + frames, no tool cancellation) they'd accept.

anna_product: Suggest scope negotiation: two-phase delivery: Phase A (6w): streaming tokens + JSON frames + clients opt-in for partialFrames. Phase B (post-pilot): cancellation semantics, quota/sla integration, and native tool connectors.

ben_sre: +1 for phased approach. We can mitigate SLO risk in Phase A by restricting max streaming duration and requiring tool-side keepalive.

jake_pm: Action items:
- mike_support: get real FinX sample payloads and acceptance checklist (due EOD Thu).
- sarah_eng: draft rough design doc (2-pager) focusing on framing, cancel semantics, and batching implications (due next Tue).
- anna_product: create GH feature request, link to pilot commitment and draft ACs (today).
- ops_bot: please create ticket and add label "customer-pilot".

ops_bot: Created issue #4521 in product/roadmap: "FinX — streaming fncall partial frames pilot" and added label customer-pilot.

mike_support: Thanks — I'll ping FinX for payloads and timeline. @mike_sales can you confirm pilot legal / security checklist?

mike_sales: On it, I’ll sync with legal and loop in account team.

anna_product: Will document scope A vs B in GH and schedule quick architecture sync with eng. Please react with :thumbsup: if you agree with phased plan.

sarah_eng: :thumbsup:

ben_sre: :thumbsup:

mike_sales: :thumbsup:

jake_pm: Setting tentative review meeting for next Wednesday 10am to align on design and pilot criteria.

mike_support: Closing loop here, will update thread when FinX confirms.
